report: Reviewed the complete claim's two requirements: associated signature checking reuses its owner interface and excludes sibling associated bodies, for trait and impl members. The sole ordinary implementation entry is LocalFnSym::sig in local_syms/fns.rs. Its local open_owner helper calls the trait or impl owner's sig, copies the binder and incorporates owner generics, Self and predicates into the function signature. The signature path checks its own parameters, return and predicates; this file contains no sibling body call in that path. Body checking is a separate method. This is direct function-path source evidence, not a proof of transitive query independence or coverage for associated types/constants. The complete associated test set is the single TODO symbols_associated_interfaces, whose empty body provides no assertions. Its explicit prerequisite is to add trace-based checks for trait and impl functions, types and constants that verify owner-interface reuse and exclude sibling-body queries; usable checking paths for each member kind and observable query traces are needed to complete that evidence. A regression that invokes a sibling body would currently escape this placeholder. The existing explicit deferral adequately preserves that verification gap and the unestablished member-kind scenarios; it does not assert full implementation or test adequacy. No new edits are requested to this unchanged accounting. Independently verified exact byte equality of both current implementation and test source files against the historical input snapshot, then reassessed the historical rationale against the current full claim, association metadata, function source and complete selected TODO test. No historical helper source was used. Captured the review policy through review read. Execution: personally ran review start, review read and the byte comparison; no behavioral tests or cargo build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator's reported build and 321 passing tests are separate baseline evidence and do not establish this deferred claim.
